title: Signed product-Hom boundary of a short exact sequence of complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small abelian category [def-sp-abelian] in a fixed Hom universe, with unbounded cochain derived category and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ be a degreewise short exact sequence of integer cochain complexes. Let $I$ be a K-injective complex, meaning that every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic, whose terms are injective objects [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $\mathsf H(X,I)^n=\prod_{r\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X^r,I^{r+n})$, as a complex of abelian groups with differential $D(f)=d_I f-(-1)^n f d_X$. Let $b:QC\to QA[1]$ be the canonical derived SES boundary, namely $-Q(\mathrm{pr}_A)Q(q)^{-1}$, where $q:\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to C$ is induced by $p$ and $\operatorname{Cone}(i)^r=B^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ with differential $(x,a)\mapsto(d_Bx+i(a),-d_Aa)$.
Then $0\to\mathsf H(C,I)\xrightarrow{p^*}\mathsf H(B,I)\xrightarrow{i^*}\mathsf H(A,I)\to0$ is short exact. Its cohomology boundary $\partial:H^0\mathsf H(A,I)\to H^1\mathsf H(C,I)$ is given, under $H^j\mathsf H(X,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal C)}(QX,QI[j])$, by
$$\partial([f])=-Q(f)[1]\circ b$$
for every chain map $f:A\to I$. Here the boundary on cohomology has the lift-differentiate convention: extend $f$ to a degree-zero graded map $g:B\to I$, factor $Dg=h p$, and take the class of $h$. This assertion holds for unbounded complexes and sequences that do not split in each degree.

proof.text: For a degree-$n$ family $u$, expand the two applications of $D$: the mixed terms have coefficients $-(-1)^n$ and $-(-1)^{n+1}$ and cancel, while the remaining terms contain $d_I^2$ or $d_X^2$. Hence $D^2u=0$. If $a:X\to Y$ is a chain map, $D(ua)=(Du)a$, since $d_Ya=ad_X$. Thus precomposition by $p$ and $i$ gives maps of the displayed abelian-group complexes, with $i^*p^*=0$. The products exist in the fixed Hom universe; no products in $\mathcal C$ are required.

source.place: Tag 0A5X (equation-cohomology-hom-complex), preceding differential formula; its coordinate calculation in an arbitrary abelian category

proof.text: Fix $n$. Precomposition by each epimorphism $p^r$ is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(C^r,I^{r+n})$. If a family $u:B^r\to I^{r+n}$ satisfies $u^ri^r=0$, the cokernel property of $p^r$ gives a unique family $v:C^r\to I^{r+n}$ with $u^r=v^rp^r$. Finally, for every family $w:A^r\to I^{r+n}$, injectivity of $I^{r+n}$ extends each $w^r$ along the monomorphism $i^r$ to $u^r:B^r\to I^{r+n}$. Choose these extensions for the set of integers $r$. This proves injectivity, middle exactness and surjectivity in every degree, hence short exactness of the Hom complexes. Only the individual $i^r$ are monomorphisms; no splitting of the original sequence has been used.

source.place: Tag 0A5X, product-Hom construction; elementary extension and cokernel argument using the stated injectivity hypothesis

proof.text: A degree-$j$ cocycle $u$ is precisely a chain map $X\to I[j]$, because $Du=0$ means $d_Iu=(-1)^ju d_X$. A boundary $Ds$, with $s$ of degree $j-1$, is null-homotopic as such a map: take the degree-$(-1)$ homotopy $(-1)^js:X\to I[j]$, whose homotopy differential is $d_I s+(-1)^jsd_X=Ds$. Conversely every such homotopy has this form. Thus the coordinate map gives $H^j\mathsf H(X,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal C)}(X,I[j])$, taking the class of $u$ to its chain-homotopy class. The shift lemma makes $I[j]$ K-injective, and the K-injective localization bijection identifies this group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal C)}(QX,QI[j])$, sending that class to $Q(u)$. This fixes the identification, in particular in degrees $0$ and $1$, without a boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $f:A\to I$ be a chain map, and use step 2 to choose a degree-zero graded extension $g:B\to I$ with $gi=f$. Since $(Dg)i=Df=0$, there is a unique degree-one $h:C\to I$ with $hp=Dg=d_Ig-gd_B$. Then $(Dh)p=D^2g=0$, and the epimorphisms $p^r$ imply $Dh=0$, so $h:C\to I[1]$ is a chain map. This is exactly the specified lift-differentiate boundary, so $\partial([f])=[h]$. To check the choices explicitly, replacing $g$ by $g+tp$ changes $h$ to $h+Dt$. If $f$ is replaced by $f+Ds$, extend the degree-$(-1)$ family $s$ to a family $t:B\to I$ using injectivity of $I^{r-1}$; the lift $g+Dt$ has unchanged differential. Therefore the cohomology class is independent both of the extension and of the representative. The same operations applied to sums show additivity.

source.place: Tag 0A5X differential formula; agent-written lift-differentiate calculation for the boundary convention stipulated in the item

proof.text: Apply the cone-projection quasi-isomorphism lemma to $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$. Its canonical morphism is exactly $q:\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to C$, $q(x,a)=p(x)$. Hence $Q(q)$ is invertible in the given derived category, and the stipulated boundary $b=-Q(\mathrm{pr}_A)Q(q)^{-1}$ is defined. The cited lemma applies to any degreewise short exact sequence, not only degreewise split sequences.

proof.text:
Both $hq$ and $f[1]\mathrm{pr}_A$ are chain maps $\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to I[1]$. Define a homotopy $H^r:\operatorname{Cone}(i)^r\to I[1]^{r-1}=I^r$ by $H^r(x,a)=g^r(x)$. On the two biproduct summands its homotopy differential is
$$d_{I[1]}H+Hd_{\operatorname{Cone}(i)}=(-d_Ig+gd_B,\,gi)=(-hp,\,f)=f[1]\mathrm{pr}_A-hq.$$
These are equations of morphisms, with $(x,a)$ denoting the two biproduct coordinates, not elements of objects of $\mathcal C$. Homotopic maps have equal image under $Q$, so $Q(h)Q(q)=Q(f)[1]Q(\mathrm{pr}_A)$. Cancel $Q(q)$ and substitute the definition of $b$ to obtain $Q(h)=-Q(f)[1]b$. Step 3 sends $[h]=\partial([f])$ to $Q(h)$, proving the claimed signed formula. All constructions are componentwise in $r$ and use no finite-support condition.
